I verified the candidate at the exact head: `pnpm typecheck` passes here; vitest cannot run in this read-only sandbox, so I relied on the author trace, which shows `pnpm test` green (18 files, 478 tests, exit 0), `format:check` and `planning:check` green, with no source edits after that run. I read the merge-tree confinement, the commit receipt, the delta-review wiring, history validation and the DIRTY publication classification against each acceptance criterion, plus the regression tests for every enumerated case.

Nothing is republished or mutated, but the cycle can spin indefinitely instead of stopping; a bounded reobservation or named stop would close it."},{"file":"scripts/dogfood/delivery-adapter.ts","line":440,"severity":"note","text":"currentMain (fetch origin <branch> plus rev-parse FETCH_HEAD) is stubbed in every test, including the delivery-adapter fixtures that have a real origin, so the only unexecuted new production path is the one that decides which main the conflict check runs against."}],"g0":"Slightly simpler: the queue already computes the authoritative answer locally via merge-tree against fetched main before delivery, so the mergeable/mergeStateStatus plumbing and the extra 'conflicted' publication state could have been dropped in favor of that single local check. The issue's fourth criterion explicitly requires reconciling the published head against remote/PR identity rather than returning publication-outcome-unknown, so the extra classification is justified here; within that constraint the shape chosen (one conflict stage reusing step(), the existing worktrees and the existing ceilings, with a ~100-line confinement module) is about as small as it can be."}
